title: Founder Legal Radar
question: A founder does not have a legal department, and the legal exposures that matter to an early company are scattered across agencies that each publish separately. The usual answer is a long checklist that nobody owns, so nothing on it ever becomes an action.
expression: Keeps a selected register of United States startup legal exposures, each one linked to the official source and labelled by source type. Every record can be moved through a review status — unreviewed, watching, ask counsel, closed — so the register becomes a set of owned decisions rather than reading. Records can be filtered by operating profile and product exposure, saved, and exported as JSON.
boundary: Deliberately selected rather than comprehensive, and educational issue spotting only. It is not legal advice, creates no attorney-client relationship, and the register does not attempt to cover every exposure a company may have.
provenance: Existing portfolio record; catalogued October 2026.

title: DEA Scheduling Monitor
question: Controlled-substance scheduling moves through the Federal Register in several document types at once, and the ones that decide anything — final rules, proposed rules, temporary orders, quotas — arrive mixed in with registrations and routine notices. Reading it raw means sorting signal from filing traffic by hand.
expression: Pulls DEA documents from the Federal Register API over a rolling 180-day window and sorts them into high-signal actions, final rules, proposed actions open for comment, and quota and temporary orders. Registrations and general notices stay available as reference categories, and the counts across views reconcile to the same document set rather than being computed separately.
boundary: Automated document discovery, not legal analysis. It tells you a document exists and what type it is; it does not tell you what it means for any particular substance, registrant, or programme.
provenance: Existing portfolio record; catalogued October 2026.

title: NSAG Lead Intelligence
question: The NSAG assessment modules each collected enquiries on their own, so there was no single place to see which modules were drawing interest, from what kinds of organisation, or whether a tier was producing anything at all.
expression: Aggregates enquiries across the NSAG modules into one dashboard, filterable by module and by organisation tier, with totals for leads, active modules and organisations represented, and a CSV export.
boundary: This is internal tooling, not a public product. It is listed here because it is part of the estate and reachable, not because there is anything on it for a visitor to use — without the key it shows only the sign-in.
provenance: Existing portfolio record; catalogued October 2026.

title: AI Governance Tracker
question: AI regulation arrives from five directions at once — FTC enforcement, state and federal legislation, bar ethics guidance, ABA guidance, and the EU AI Act — and no single feed covers them together. Anyone tracking it by hand is reading five newsletters and hoping none of them lapsed.
expression: Runs a scheduled sweep every Monday, files what it finds into those five categories, and publishes the result as a dashboard and a JSON endpoint. The API returns a collection-health block alongside the documents: last sweep time, age in days, failed-search count, newest item date, and a stale flag that trips after two missed cycles. A stale register is shown as stale rather than presented as the current picture.
boundary: This is a collector, not a verifier. Results come from automated search, and the corpus includes secondary reporting about enforcement actions as well as primary documents. Nothing in it is a legal conclusion or a substitute for reading the source.
provenance: Existing portfolio record; catalogued October 2026.

title: Legal AI Guidance Monitor
question: When a court sanctions a lawyer for filing fabricated citations, the coverage travels much further than the order. Practitioners need the actual authority — the ABA opinion, the state bar guidance, the standing order, the published sanctions opinion — separated from commentary about it.
expression: Holds a hand-verified register of primary authorities on lawyers' use of generative AI: ABA Formal Opinion 512, four state and city bar opinions, two Middle District of Florida standing orders, and a published Ninth Circuit sanctions opinion. Each carries its jurisdiction, authority type, verification date and a link to the official source. A separate weekly sweep searches official domains for new candidates; anything it finds is filed as an unverified candidate and stays that way until a reviewer opens the document and confirms the characterisation. The two tiers are never merged.
boundary: The eight verified authorities were confirmed on 17 August 2026. The discovery sweep has not completed since 10 August 2026 and the site reports itself stale; the verified register is unaffected by that, but recent guidance may be missing. Not legal advice.
provenance: Existing portfolio record; catalogued October 2026.

title: Psych Ops Source Watch
question: Psychedelic regulation moves through state programme portals and rulemaking pages that publish on no fixed schedule. Most trackers in the space blur an official rule change together with a press release or an advocacy claim.
expression: Watches six verified official source endpoints — Oregon Health Authority psilocybin services, Colorado natural medicine, and four others — on a weekly cycle. Every candidate a query returns is put through a source policy before it is shown; on the most recent sweep, seven candidates passed and forty-one were rejected as noise. The page reports per-category sweep state, how many sources were healthy, degraded or failed, and how many days old the last successful sweep is.
boundary: Screened candidates are unreviewed. A record in the source registry means the endpoint is monitored, not that something new was published there. Not legal advice.
provenance: Existing portfolio record; catalogued October 2026.

title: Platform Moderation Evidence Lab
question: Arguments about platform moderation of drug-related speech run on a mix of evidence types that get quoted interchangeably: an Oversight Board decision, a regulator's inquiry, a platform's own statement, and an advocacy group's allegation are not the same kind of fact, but they are cited as though they were.
expression: Keeps a source-linked register in which every record states four things separately — the claim, what its source actually establishes, the evidentiary boundary, and the verification date. An overturned Oversight Board decision is recorded as a documented reversal in an individual case, with an explicit note that it does not establish a platform-wide pattern, a motive, or a legal violation. Review state is kept in the visitor's browser.
boundary: Bounded by design — it covers the documented public record, not the full universe of moderation decisions. Priority flags are local triage, not findings.
provenance: Existing portfolio record; catalogued October 2026.

title: Culture Intelligence Monitor

title: Drug Market Transition Evidence Lab

title: Entheogen Atlas
question: The popular history of psychedelics is built on a handful of dramatic claims that have quietly failed replication, and they are repeated because the confirmed record and the contested one are told in the same voice. expression: Assembles archaeology, neuroscience, legal history, phenomenology and religious use into one atlas anchored on the oldest chemically confirmed use of a psychedelic — peyote from Shumla Cave, radiocarbon dated to 3780–3660 cal BC and shown by GC-MS to contain mescaline. Older claims are carried where they are serious, but held on an explicit evidence ladder rather than folded into a single headline figure. A separate evidence register and governance page record how each rung is assigned.
boundary: Development and availability are described in the underlying portfolio record.
provenance: Existing portfolio record; catalogued October 2026.

title: Microdosing Knowledge Atlas
question: Thirty-four years of one researcher's recorded public output — talks, interviews, papers, broadcasts — is scattered across platforms that come and go, and there is no way to see the shape of the whole or to know which references still resolve.

title: Color Vision Field Guide

title: Evidence to Experience
question: Can one evidence base survive every translation?
expression: A controlled demonstration translating a primary-source corpus and claim ledger into materials for different audiences, with recorded review decisions and evaluation of accuracy, completeness and consistency.
boundary: A proposed design sprint and test. No clinical effect, tool performance or successful pilot is asserted.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Follow the Fact
question: What changed between the original reporting and the AI answer?
expression: A public experience for tracing a claim through reporting, retrieval, citation and transformation. Readers could examine lost context, misplaced categories and the route back to the originating source.
boundary: A feasibility proposal and product question. It does not establish an implemented publisher partnership or a working attribution service.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Public Agency Lab
question: How can people trace, test and challenge information in an AI-mediated world?
expression: A proposed research and prototyping program connecting media literacy, AI literacy, accessibility and public agency. Follow the Fact was its first proposed test.
boundary: An institutional proposal related to Follow the Fact, not a separate delivered organization.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Care Trust Infrastructure
question: How can screening become explainable, contestable and connected to longer-term evidence?
expression: An evidence, equity and trust architecture connecting assessment boundaries, human review, data uses, referral decisions and longitudinal outcomes in psychedelic-care workflows.
boundary: A proposed architecture and pilot. Clinical validity, reimbursement and regulatory status remain unestablished; the gallery offers no screening or medical advice.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Research to Practice
question: How can an emerging field connect scientific questions, practitioner education and the people whose experiences are missing?
expression: A proposed operating system for sex-aware science and gender-responsive practice: research prioritization, claim governance, partnerships and knowledge translation, tested through one flagship research priority.
boundary: A proposed research-to-practice institution and bounded pilot, not a clinical service or evidence of treatment efficacy.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Human Intelligence OS
question: How can a brand preserve the depth of human observation as it grows?
expression: A governed institutional memory connecting cultural observation, identity research, creative experimentation, circularity evidence and responsible AI across creative, product, sustainability and leadership decisions.
boundary: A strategic proposal. The research system and pilot require validation; no brand adoption or commercial outcome is claimed.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: The Entertainment Trust Layer
question: What lets AI-native filmmaking become repeatable, explainable and commercially usable?
expression: A proposed operating layer connecting production learning, rights and provenance, market intelligence, partner expectations, institutional knowledge and creator education.
boundary: A proposed founding engagement. Existing films, underlying intellectual property and other creators’ work are not claimed as RN’s.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Author Intelligence System
question: What if finishing a book created the infrastructure for the next one?
expression: A proposed system joining manuscript completion, research, publication, audience learning, multimedia, speaking, education and future opportunities. Workstreams would activate in bounded phases.
boundary: RN conceived the proposed system. The author’s underlying manuscript, ideas and existing intellectual property remain the author’s; no publication or commercial result is claimed.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Experiment to Institution
question: How can the learning from a public legal-AI experiment become a reusable institutional asset?
expression: A proposed evidence corpus and governance system capturing workflows, failures, evaluation, practitioner intelligence and research so they can support training, advisory work and future products.
boundary: A proposed research and knowledge-system contribution. The original experiment and its creator’s frameworks are not RN’s work.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Human Capacity & Responsible Technology Institute
question: What if the first technology decision were to diagnose the actual constraint?
expression: A proposed place-based institute combining applied research, policy support, workforce development and implementation. A Phase 0 study would test public value, institutional home, governance and funding before creation.
boundary: A founding proposal and feasibility pathway, not an established institute. An existing institution, nontechnical intervention or no new structure could be the appropriate result.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Regulatory Change to Action
question: How can one regulatory development become consistent, reviewable work across several professional teams?
expression: A proposed source-grounded system connecting controlling authority, versions, economic evidence, cross-practice implications and review history to an internal brief and an approved downstream output.
boundary: A bounded pilot proposal using public, synthetic or specifically authorized information. Attorney and specialist review remains necessary.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: People-First AI Governance
question: What connects a legal requirement to the decision someone actually makes at work?
expression: A proposed operating system for regulated small businesses connecting authority, AI uses, affected people, controls, evidence, education and change, with a governed translation layer between legal and technical work.
boundary: A proposed offering. It is not a legal opinion, compliance certification or claim of implementation.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Partner Pathway + Evidence
question: How does a promising opportunity become a project with an owner and a usable record?
expression: A proposed pilot following one or two opportunities through understanding, classification, routing, disposition, handoff and learning. Outputs would include an intake instrument, authority matrix and decision record.
boundary: A pilot proposal that preserves existing institutional authority. It does not claim the pathway has been adopted.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Creator Rights Editorial Partnership
question: How can a creator understand what they own without becoming a legal specialist?
expression: A proposed plain-language editorial collaboration joining RN’s research, writing and production with optional practitioner review and a recurring creator-IP question format.
boundary: A collaboration proposal. Practitioner participation, review and credit require express agreement; no affiliation is implied.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Capability & Choice
question: When should a capability become visible—and when should it remain private?
expression: A proposed participant-controlled research mechanism examining disclosure, opportunity, recognition, compensation and possible harms. Capability, willingness to disclose and permission to use would remain separate decisions.
boundary: Part of the Institutions of One research proposal. No universal score, automatic ranking or manager-facing employment database is claimed.
provenance: Recovered authored proposal; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Private Proposal Studio
question: How can an individualized proposal reach the intended reader while preserving the approved version and a clear boundary around access?
expression: A reusable proposal-delivery architecture connecting an approved content snapshot, recipient authorization, revocable access and release verification. The recovered implementation separates proposal presentation, generation, access control and certification.
boundary: Recovered prototype with locally tested synthetic records. The archived record leaves live deployment and authorization certification pending; this entry does not claim a deployed or independently audited security product.
provenance: Recovered implementation archive and accompanying documentation; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: Fieldwork That Outlasts the Trip
question: What would make the learning, relationships and commitments from a short expedition remain useful after everyone leaves?
expression: A before, during and after field research system: source-linked preparation, consent-aware interviews and visual records, daily synthesis separating observation from inference, a rights-aware archive, and follow-up at 30 and 90 days. Reported features, films and decision briefs would draw from the same evidence base.
boundary: A proposed contribution and production model, not a delivered expedition or confirmed engagement. Scope, local priorities, consent, cultural authority, editorial independence and publication rights would be agreed with participants and partners.
provenance: Recovered authored contribution note and proposal website source; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.

title: The Body Data Story
question: How could a health-data service become a story people recognize in their own lives?
expression: A proposed creative partnership connecting people, data and health through audience research, content specimens, distribution and measurement. The surviving visual studies frame real people and their questions as the starting point for stories and relationships.
boundary: Recovered visual proposal studies, not a delivered campaign or a claim of ownership of any measurement technology. The complete underlying research and production scope have not been recovered; no health or commercial outcome is asserted.
provenance: Recovered visual proposal studies and their extracted text; catalogued October 2026. Catalogue date is not a first-conception date.
